methods: Independent source tracing of MvpApp, CvCheck, AuthContext, check-draft, JobLoop, LoopPacketPreview, LoopWorkingDraft and document-loading boundaries.
Reviewed existing journey-test coverage without using prior audit reports.
Ran two targeted synthetic component observations with fictional data, maxWorkers=1; both passed. An initial launcher attempt was stopped before using the direct runner.
No runtime edits, network/account writes, services or private candidate data.
not_tested: Live production routes or real authenticated accounts
Production OAuth timing or storage behavior across actual browser refresh

criteria.name: State ownership and preservation
criteria.evidence: CvCheck 98/271 and JobLoop 93/287: two reproduced losses plus an omitted tracking-draft class despite explicit recovery machinery.

criteria.name: Async and authentication correctness
criteria.evidence: JobLoop 238/306 and LoopPacketPreview use owner/generation/hash/abort guards; CvCheck 98 ignores authLoading for recovery.

criteria.name: Accessible forms and navigation
criteria.evidence: CvCheck 136/228/379 associates validation and focus; JobLoop 60 provides labelled fields and help; real assistive-technology operation untested.

criteria.name: Component architecture and testability
criteria.evidence: Pure check-draft/evidence modules and journey tests; CvCheck 98–125 holds many coupled state values and transition functions duplicate resets.

criteria.name: Loading and render efficiency
criteria.evidence: MvpApp lazy route imports; cv-extraction 43–48 and document-export 44/65 dynamically load heavy libraries; no device profiling measured.

strengths: Lazy working routes and document libraries defer heavy loading.
Guest approval is bound to exact inputs; review and saving remain separate explicit actions.
Private Loop async work is guarded by owner, generation and packet hashes with abortable downloads.
Labelled controls, focus management, alerts/status and extensive journey tests provide a sound incremental base.

findings.problem: An explicitly consented signed-in /check refresh draft is deleted while authentication is still loading, before the same owner is restored.

evidence.detail: Synthetic fictional-owner remount with user=null/loading=true removes recovery storage; resolving the same owner leaves the role empty. Assertion passed.
Session begins null while loading is true.
Recovery is read once from user?.id ?? null before auth settles; line 225 writes the initial state.
An owner mismatch causes stored recovery removal at line 108.

findings.recommendation: Delay owner-bound recovery hydration and retention writes until auth ownership is established, preserving immediate guest usage and owner isolation.
acceptance_criteria: Delayed same-owner bootstrap restores the exact consented draft, step and page preference.
Different-owner bootstrap never exposes the retained draft.
Guest recovery remains usable and recovered approval stays cleared.
findings.cost_effect: No paid services or model calls; protects completed user review work.

findings.problem: Navigating back to an unchanged vacancy and rechecking replaces final CV edits with source wording without confirmation or undo.

evidence.detail: Synthetic test edits the final CV, navigates to One vacancy without changing inputs, rechecks, and observes source text replacing the edit. Assertion passed.
runCheck substitutes sourceText for reviewedText and line 273 overwrites the working draft.
confirmCv also replaces reviewedText with sourceText; backward navigation is unrestricted at line 248.

findings.recommendation: Separate initial composition from evidence recomputation; preserve working final edits on unchanged backward/forward navigation and confirm source-triggered replacement with undo. Centralize related transitions in a small reducer or workflow hook.
acceptance_criteria: Same-input setup navigation preserves exact final edits and confidentiality removals.
Source replacement requires explicit confirmation and offers undo.
Changed inputs invalidate approval, preview and save consent.
findings.cost_effect: No additional provider cost; reduces repeated editing and accidental return of removed wording.

findings.problem: Existing-opportunity notes, dates and status edits are absent from unsaved-work detection and route recovery; server changes can remount their local editors.

evidence.detail: OpportunityRow owns tracking edits in local useState; no dirty/draft callback is present.
hasUnsavedDraft covers profile, claims and new-opportunity fields only; retention at 289 omits existing tracking edits.
OpportunityRow key includes saved status, followUpAt and notes, so refreshed changes remount the editor.
LoopWorkingDraft has no existing-opportunity tracking draft collection.

findings.recommendation: Own dirty tracking drafts by stable opportunity ID in the parent recovery contract, include them in navigation protection, and reconcile refreshed rows while retaining fresh status attestation requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Route return restores unsaved notes and date and requires fresh status attestation.
Account changes clear the tracking drafts.
A concurrent saved-record change does not silently overwrite dirty edits and offers explicit reconciliation.
findings.cost_effect: No additional backend storage required; consistent continuity within existing memory policy.

open_questions: What authentication bootstrap latency occurs on actual /check refreshes in the supported browsers?
How often do pilot professionals leave the tracking editor to consult help or employer pages?
Which mobile devices establish an appropriate evidence-rendering performance budget?
do_not_build_now: Framework migration or a new global state platform.
New paid model/search integrations before continuity defects are fixed.
Broad extraction of every large component without transition-level acceptance tests.
